method.description: Identity resolution only. The assigned identifier was tested against what Florida Rule of Criminal Procedure 3.989 actually prescribes, read end to end in the current official compilation, against the Supreme Court opinion that last amended it, against the statutes the rule implements, and against the component declaration in the integrated Florida memo that introduced the identifier. No component was rebound, no legal design was altered and no edition was mutated.
method.verificationNote: The rule was extracted and scanned independently of any summary: the compilation's text was searched for the rule heading, the span from 'RULE 3.989.' to the start of 'RULE 3.9895.' was isolated, and the subdivision headings, form captions and continuation-term scan were computed directly on that span.

questionPresented: Does the document the repository calls FL-RULE-3.989-CONTINUATION exist, and if so what is it?

identityResolution.confidenceBasis: This is not a failure to find. The rule was read end to end and it has no continuation construct of any kind. The negative is affirmative.
identityResolution.isALocallyCreatedDerivative: partly — see componentConditionAnalysis; half of what the component describes is a local circuit packet convention, which is a local derivative and not a statewide official form
evidence: Florida Rule of Criminal Procedure 3.989 sets out four forms and none of them is a continuation. Its subdivisions are (a) Sworn Statement in Support of Petition, (b) Order to Expunge, (c) Order to Seal and (d) Petition to Expunge or Seal.

A case-insensitive scan of the rule's complete span for continuation, continued, additional, attach, more space, second sheet, schedule, exhibit, supplement, if needed, insufficient, reverse side, addendum and annex returns zero matches. Not one of those words appears anywhere inside Rule 3.989.

The rule's forms are single-arrest instruments with narrative blanks such as .....(charges) and .....(date). There is no repeating block, no 'if more space is needed' instruction and no attachment mechanism.
Nothing in the adopted edition matches. The authoritative blocker ledger records controllingLibraryRow 'MASTER_ASSET_MANIFEST.csv:no-matching-row' for this documentId.

The identifier is bound to exactly one component in the entire corpus, fl-expunction-continuation-6. The three sibling tracks that use the same Rule 3.989 forms — fl-sealing, fl-10yr-bridge and fl-trafficking — have no continuation component at all. If the rule prescribed a continuation, those tracks would need it too.
The component carries no notes and no provenance block, while every other component on the same track carries notes. It is the only unsourced component on the track.

The identifier's shape is the signature of the defect: a rule number with a role word suffixed onto it. This repository has already resolved one identifier formed exactly that way — CO's JDF-417-ORDER — as a normalization artefact.

statutoryTreatmentOfAdditionalArrests.why_recorded: It is the substantive need behind the first half of the component's condition, and it establishes that Florida answers that need somewhere other than a form page.
statutoryTreatmentOfAdditionalArrests.statute: § 943.0585(4)(c), Fla. Stat., mirrored verbatim for sealing at § 943.059(4)(c)
statutoryTreatmentOfAdditionalArrests.verbatim: The court may order expunction of a criminal history record pertaining to one arrest or one incident of alleged criminal activity only, except that the court may order the expunction of a criminal history record pertaining to more than one arrest if the additional arrests directly relate to the original arrest. If the court intends to order the expunction of records pertaining to such additional arrests, such intent must be specified in the order. A criminal justice agency may not expunge any record pertaining to such additional arrests if the order to expunge does not articulate the intention of the court to expunge a record pertaining to more than one arrest.
statutoryTreatmentOfAdditionalArrests.consequence: Florida handles additional arrests as language the judge writes into the order, and an agency may not act on additional arrests unless the order articulates that intent. It is an order-drafting requirement, not a continuation sheet. Rule 3.989(b) and (c) provide no blank for it, so a drafter must add it to the order text.
statutoryTreatmentOfAdditionalArrests.correctPlacementIfTheNeedIsReal: Rule 3.989(b) or (c) order-body language, plus a separate FDLE certificate of eligibility per arrest. Not a new page and not a new document identity.
statutoryTreatmentOfAdditionalArrests.notDecidedHere: Whether that is what the component was reaching for. Establishing the component's originating requirement is a legal-design question and is outside this assignment.
statutoryTreatmentOfAdditionalArrests.noAttachmentLanguageInEitherStatute: Neither § 943.0585 nor § 943.059 mentions attachments, additional sheets, schedules or continuation pages. What must accompany the petition is a valid FDLE certificate of eligibility and the petitioner's sworn statement.

likelyConfusionSource.candidate: FDLE Form 40-021, Application for a Certificate of Eligibility
likelyConfusionSource.why: It is the only document in the entire Florida expunction stack that carries an additional-charges construct.
likelyConfusionSource.construct: Two numbered 1-to-8 repeating blocks — one on page 1 under a single Arresting Agency header for Date(s) of Arrest and Charge(s) Description, and one on the state attorney's written certified statement page for Charge(s) Description, Statute Violation, Case Number and Action.
likelyConfusionSource.butItIsNotAContinuation: Zero matches for continuation, additional page, more space or attach anywhere in the form. The blocks are multiple charges within one arrest, not multiple cases across a continuation sheet.
likelyConfusionSource.andItIsNotARule3989Form: It is an FDLE administrative application filed before any court filing, incorporated by reference into Fla. Admin. Code R. 11C-7.006. It is not promulgated by the Supreme Court.
likelyConfusionSource.alreadySeparatelyBound: The same track already binds it at fl-expunction-primary-filing-1 under the identity FDLE-CERTIFICATE-OF-ELIGIBILITY-APPLICATION. Binding it a second time as a continuation would duplicate one document under two identities.
likelyConfusionSource.statusNote: Recorded because it is the one place the '1 through 8' shape actually exists, and because a later reader will otherwise rediscover it and mistake it for the missing continuation. It is not asserted as the component's origin, and it does not license rebinding anything.

mayAnotherPageOrFormLegallySubstitute.why: Rule 3.989 prescribes four forms and a court filing must use them. There is no fifth form to substitute in, no continuation to attach, and a local circuit cover sheet is not a Supreme Court form. The statutory route for additional arrests is order-body language, which is text inside form (b) or (c) rather than a substitute document.

sourceAvailabilityAndStructure.eligibleForLaterMaterializationWhy: Materialization presupposes a document. There is nothing to materialize and no receipt should ever be written for this identity.

terminalDispositionDetail.why: The narrowest disposition the evidence supports. It is not unresolved_identity: the question was answered, and answered in the negative with affirmative evidence. It is not identity_established_binary_unavailable, which is what the edition currently records — that phrasing asserts a document exists and is merely unobtained, which is the opposite of what is true. It is not superseded or retired, because the document was never issued. It is not official_download_automation_blocked: the Bar compilation's 403 to a default agent was worked around and the rule was read in full. The identifier names nothing, and the component that carries it needs re-scoping rather than acquisition.
terminalDispositionDetail.acquisitionRequiredRationale: No issuer interaction can produce a document the Supreme Court of Florida has never promulgated. acquire:FL:fl-rule-3-989-continuation should not remain an open download job.
